name: Header
summary: Header sections for the AhaSlides marketing sites: four heroes and one page header, each with its own preview, switches and paste-and-run code.
highlights: Five layouts on one page, one per structure: Hero split, Hero stacked, Hero card, Hero split form and Page header. Colour, alignment, picture and call-to-action differences are switches on the layout, not separate layouts

Every layout has a White / Accent / Vivid Pink surface switch: add the layout's own --accent class (the pale pink bgAccent surface over white) or --brand class (Vivid Pink on the DS Splash background)

An optional G2 reviews row (the G2 logo in a white card, five stars, 4.8 and the review count), on by default, on the three heroes whose copy block holds the call to action; a G2 reviews switch next to the other switches turns it off on the preview
layoutsIntro: Each layout is its own block: the class names below are scoped per layout, so any number of them can sit in one page.

guidance.title: Choosing a header
guidance.intro: Pick the header from the goal of the page, then check the points below. The layouts further down carry a "Use for" line.

points.title: One goal, one primary button
points.text: Each page has one goal and one primary button: one Vivid Pink primary and at most one white secondary. Never two primaries, as the Button rule allows one primary per view. On the Vivid Pink surface the button is variant="secondary"; on White and Accent it is the primary. The per-surface switch is the data-variant-<state> hook on the button, so paste the snippet for the surface you use.

points.title: Layout by page goal
points.text: Sign-ups (home, campaign, landing): Hero split or Hero stacked with the Email form call to action, or Hero card. Use Hero split form only when you need more than an email. Feature pages: Hero split with the Bleed picture for a wide screenshot, or Hero stacked when the product screen is the proof. Content and listing pages (blog, templates, help): Page header, with no button on purpose; turn its Buttons on only when the page has one clear action. Brand or campaign banners: any hero on the Vivid Pink surface.

points.title: Copy
points.text: Write an outcome-led headline of about ten words or fewer and a one-sentence lead. Label the button with a verb and the outcome. Put a risk reducer under the button, for example "Free plan, no card needed".

points.title: Above the fold
points.text: The headline, the button and the visual are visible without scrolling at 1280 by 720 and on mobile. Use a real AhaSlides screenshot, not a stock photo. The badge slot (the Badge switch) carries news or a short label, not decoration. For proof, keep the G2 reviews row (the G2 logo, stars and the 4.8 rating), which sits under the call to action on the three heroes and is on by default. In Hero stacked the picture is shown whole at its own ratio at every width, never cropped with object-fit cover (rule W6): supply the screenshot at the ratio you want shown.

points.title: Colour
points.text: Colour rule 3.5 keeps the first screen of a product-app screen white, but a web page built from full-width sections may open with a Vivid Pink header (it is one of the two Vivid Pink sections of rule 3.4). Follow it with a full white section, never another coloured one. A Vivid Pink header always carries the DS Splash background (right when the copy is beside a picture or left-aligned with no picture, centre when the copy is centred or a picture fills the width), never a flat pink fill or hand-drawn hooks.

points.title: One H1 per page
points.text: A page has one h1. If a second hero sits on the page, its headline becomes an h2.

points.title: Measure
points.text: Track the click on the primary button. A/B test the headline before you change the layout.

points.title: Background
points.text: Every layout has a White / Accent / Vivid Pink switch: add the layout's own --accent class (for example aha-header-section-hero-split--accent) to lay the pale pink Accent background (bgAccent) over white, or its --brand class for Vivid Pink. On Hero card the switch colours the panel, not the page. Accent and Vivid Pink are alternatives, never combined. Never place an Accent or Vivid Pink header next to another coloured section.

points.title: Hero video
points.text: A hero can carry a video instead of the image (the optional Video slot below, off by default): a real <video> with controls, a poster that is a real screenshot, an English captions track and a download link as fallback. It never autoplays, never loops and never starts with sound, so it is safe under prefers-reduced-motion; the native controls are keyboard reachable. The video box takes the clip's own aspect ratio from the width and height attributes (set them to the clip's real pixel size), so a wide 2.12:1 demo and a 16:9 clip both fill the box with no dark bands and no crop; a height cap keeps a tall clip from taking over the hero.

layouts.name: Hero split
layouts.summary: Hero with the copy on the left and a picture on the right. Rebuilt in our own HTML and CSS from DS tokens and the DS input styles, every button an ; every picture is a real of the DS placeholder image. No third-party code, text or assets.
layouts.useFor: Most landing, feature and campaign pages. Switch the picture to Bleed for a wide product screenshot that runs off the right edge, and the call to action to Email form for a sign-up page with one goal.

layouts.name: Page header
layouts.summary: Page header section with a section label, a title and supporting text, left-aligned, centred or with the actions on the right (stacked under 992px), and an optional row of tabs. Rebuilt in DS tokens and the DS tab styles, every button an <aha-button>; framework-free. Layout idea from a public header-section gallery, no third-party code or assets.
layouts.useFor: Content and listing pages (blog, templates, help) with no button on purpose; turn Buttons on and choose Space between only when the page has one clear action, and Tabs on for pages that switch between views.

video.label: Video slot
video.howToTurnOn: Replace the layout's with the video html and add the css once, replacing {{c}} with the layout class. Set the width and height attributes to the clip's real pixel size: the slot takes that ratio. Off by default: the layout html and css leave it out. Never add autoplay, muted autoplay or loop.
